title: Clip-On Book Lights for Older Eyes: Easy Gifts for Reading in Bed or in a Favorite Chair
subtitle: A small light that clips to the page can make reading easier, as long as you choose one that fits the reader's hands, eyes and habits.
excerpt: Our eyes need more light as we age, and a clip-on book light puts it right on the page. Here is what to look for, two affordable options, and what these little lights cannot do.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: If you love to read in bed or in a cozy chair, you may have noticed that the words seem fainter than they used to. That is not your imagination. The Macular Society, a UK charity for people with sight loss, notes that a person of 60 needs about three times as much light as someone in their twenties.

A book light is a small, inexpensive fix. It clips onto your book or magazine and shines right where you are reading. CNN Underscored lists clip-on lights as a common pick for reading in bed. It also makes a thoughtful, low-cost gift for a parent or friend who reads every night.

A book light clips to your book or magazine and aims a small light at the page. Some, like the Carson PageGlow below, spread several small LED lights across the page. Others, like the Carson FlexNeck, have a flexible lamp head you can aim where you need it.

Power comes in two ways as well. Some run on regular AAA batteries that you swap out when they run low. Others have a built-in battery that you recharge with a USB cable, the same kind of cord many phones use. Neither is better for everyone. Batteries are simple but cost a little over time. Rechargeable lights save on batteries, but you have to remember to plug them in.
"Readers benefit more from book lights that offer adjustable brightness modes rather than having just one fixed output." (CNN Underscored, book light buying guide)

items: Adjustable brightness. A dimmer lets you pick a comfortable level instead of living with one fixed output.
A clip that suits the hands. Clip-on lights use spring clips, and hands with arthritis may find them hard to open. Try the clip yourself before you give it.

The right power type. For AAA models, buy a pack of batteries to give with the light, since they are not included. For rechargeable models, check that the reader has a USB charger or wall plug and will remember to charge it.
Size and weight. The notes list 4 oz for the PageGlow and 1.6 oz for the FlexNeck. Check the listed ounces and dimensions so the light suits the reader and the book.

Returns. Whatever the seller, look for a clear return policy before buying, especially for a gift, in case the clip or brightness does not suit. We have not checked MaxiAids' return policy, so read it first.
No monthly fees. Neither of the lights below has a subscription or monthly fee, though AAA batteries are an ongoing cost.

sections.content: Where you point the light matters as much as how bright it is. The Macular Society's lighting advice puts it simply:
"Task lamps need to be positioned below eye level, shining onto the task, not into your eyes." (The Macular Society, lighting guide)
For a book light, that means angling the lamp down at the page so you never see the bulb itself. The same guide suggests keeping some background light on in the room to reduce glare.

If your light has brightness settings, start low and turn it up until the print looks crisp. If you are giving one as a gift, put the batteries in or charge it first, so it works the moment the wrapping comes off.

A book light lights one page, not a room. It will not replace a good lamp for sewing, paying bills or reading very fine print. People with macular degeneration or other low vision may need a larger, brighter task lamp instead, and it is worth asking an eye doctor what would help. A book light is not a medical device and does not treat any eye condition.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: A little light can bring back the simple pleasure of a chapter before sleep. Pick one that matches the reader's hands and habits, aim it at the page, and enjoy the next good book.
